'''Azam Niroomand-Rad''' ({{langx|fa|اعظم نیرومند راد}}; born 1947) is an Iranian-American [[medical physicist]] specializing in radiation oncology physics and [[Dosimetry|radiation dosimetry]]. She is professor emerita of radiation medicine at [[Georgetown University Medical Center]] and an honorary professor of medical physics at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].<ref name="iomp-webinar">{{cite web |title=IOMP School Webinars 2023 |url=https://www.iomp.org/iomp-school-webinars-2023/ |access-date=3 November 2026 |publisher=International Organization for Medical Physics}}</ref><ref name="aapm2006">{{cite web |date=31 July 2006 |title=American Association of Physicists in Medicine Awards Ceremony, July 31, 2006 |url=https://aapm.org/org/history/2006AwardsCeremonyProgram.pdf |access-date=3 November 2026 |publisher=American Association of Physicists in Medicine}}</ref> From 2003 to 2006 she was president of the [[International Organization for Medical Physics]] (IOMP), the first woman to hold the post.<ref name="iomp-webinar" /><ref name="mpi-pioneer">{{cite journal |last1=Niroomand-Rad |first1=Azam |last2=Tabakov |first2=Slavik |year=2023 |title=History of Pioneer Women in Medical Physics |url=http://mpijournal.org/pdf/2023-HE-09/MPI-2022-HE-09-1042.pdf |journal=Medical Physics International |issue=History Edition 9}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Niroomand-Rad was born in [[Tehran]], Iran, in 1947.<ref name="mpi-pioneer" /> She moved to the United States as a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright]] scholarship student<ref name="iomp-webinar" /> and earned a Bachelor of Science in mathematics, summa cum laude, from the State University of New York at Albany in 1970. She received a PhD in atomic and molecular physics from [[Michigan State University]] in 1978,<ref name="aapm2006" /><ref name="iupesm">{{cite web |title=Fellow Profile: Azam Niroomand-Rad |url=https://www.iomp.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/Table-35-FIUPESM-2022.pdf |access-date=9 May 2026 |publisher=International Union for Physical and Engineering Sciences in Medicine}}</ref> and then trained in medical physics at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].<ref name="iupesm" />

== Career ==
Niroomand-Rad worked as a clinical radiation oncology physicist and academic at [[Georgetown University Medical Center]] in Washington, D.C., where she served as clinical physics director in the Department of Radiation Medicine.<ref name="aapm2006" /><ref name="mpw2005">{{cite journal |date=December 2005 |title=President's Message |url=https://www.iomp.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/18-mpwdec2005.pdf |journal=Medical Physics World |publisher=International Organization for Medical Physics |volume=21 |issue=2}}</ref> She later became an honorary professor of medical physics at the University of Wisconsin–Madison.<ref name="iomp-webinar" />

She was vice-president of the IOMP before serving as its president from 2003 to 2006.<ref name="mpi-pioneer" /><ref name="mpw2005" /> She founded the AAPM/IOMP International Scientific Exchange Programs (ISEP), which ran training courses in medical physics for developing countries; the first was held in [[Islamabad]], Pakistan, in 1992, and later courses took place in Asia, Africa, and the Middle East.<ref name="iomp-webinar" /><ref name="iomp-annex">{{cite journal |year=2022 |title=Annex: IOMP History Tables |url=http://mpijournal.org/pdf/2022-SI-07/MPI-2022-SI-07-p759.pdf |journal=Medical Physics International}}</ref> She also co-directed the first Cuba–USA International Conference on Medical Physics.<ref name="iomp-annex" /> According to the IOMP, her work in its leadership included seeking recognition of medical physics as a profession by the [[International Labour Organization]] and establishing IOMP awards.<ref name="iomp-webinar" /> In 2003 she took part in an [[International Atomic Energy Agency]] expert activity in [[Amman]], Jordan.<ref name="mpi-pioneer" />

She edited the IOMP bulletin ''Medical Physics World'' from 1994 to 2000<ref name="mpi-pioneer" /> and was an associate editor of the journal ''[[Medical Physics (journal)|Medical Physics]]''.<ref name="iupesm" /> Within the [[American Association of Physicists in Medicine]] (AAPM) she served on committees and task groups, including Task Group 235,<ref name="aapm2006" /><ref name="tg235">{{cite journal |last1=Niroomand-Rad |first1=Azam |last2=Chiu-Tsao |first2=Sou-Tung |last3=Grams |first3=Michael P. |date=December 2020 |title=Report of AAPM Task Group 235 Radiochromic Film Dosimetry: An Update to TG-55 |journal=Medical Physics |volume=47 |issue=12 |pages=5986–6025 |doi=10.1002/mp.14497 |pmid=32990328}}</ref> and in 1998 she presented the results of an AAPM survey of women in medical physics.<ref name="aapm1998">{{cite web |year=1998 |title=40th Annual Meeting, American Association of Physicists in Medicine – Program |url=https://www.aapm.org/meetings/july98/98am.pdf |access-date=3 November 2026 |publisher=American Association of Physicists in Medicine}}</ref>

== Research ==
Her research has covered electron beam dosimetry, including total skin electron irradiation,<ref name="tseb1986">{{cite journal |last1=Niroomand-Rad |first1=A. |last2=Gillin |first2=M. T. |last3=Komaki |first3=R. |last4=Kline |first4=R. W. |last5=Grimm |first5=D. F. |date=March 1986 |title=Dose distribution in total skin electron beam irradiation using the six-field technique |journal=International Journal of Radiation Oncology, Biology, Physics |volume=12 |issue=3 |pages=415–419 |doi=10.1016/0360-3016(86)90361-5 |pmid=3082810}}</ref> calibration of high-energy photon and electron beams,<ref name="tg51">{{cite journal |last1=Rodgers |first1=J. E. |last2=Niroomand-Rad |first2=A. |last3=Lundsten |first3=M. |date=August 2000 |title=Comment on clinical implementation of the AAPM's Task Group-51 protocol for calibration of high-energy photon and electron beams |journal=Medical Physics |volume=27 |issue=8 |pages=1995–1996 |doi=10.1118/1.1287647 |pmid=10984245}}</ref> and [[radiochromic film]] dosimetry. She was first author of the report of AAPM Task Group 235, which updated the earlier TG-55 recommendations on radiochromic film dosimetry.<ref name="tg235" /> She has also written on the history of medical physics education in Iran.<ref name="physmed2017">{{cite journal |last1=Mahdavi |first1=Seyed Rabi |last2=Rasuli |first2=Behrouz |last3=Niroomand-Rad |first3=Azam |date=April 2017 |title=Education and training of medical physics in Iran: The past, the present and the future |journal=Physica Medica |volume=36 |pages=66–72 |doi=10.1016/j.ejmp.2017.03.007 |pmid=28410688}}</ref>

She is a co-inventor of U.S. Patent 6,665,555, granted in 2003 and assigned to Georgetown University, for a method of delivering [[Radiosurgery|stereotactic radiosurgery]] to lesions of the spine.<ref name="patent">{{cite patent|country=US|number=6665555|title=Radiosurgery methods that utilize stereotactic methods to precisely deliver high dosages of radiation especially to the spine|status=patent|pubdate=2003-12-16|inventor=Henderson, Fraser C.; Rodgers, James; Niroomand-Rad, Azam; Cleary, Kevin; Dritschilo, Anatoly; Der, Leon|assign1=Georgetown University School of Medicine}}</ref><ref name="aapm2006" />
